name: Documentation Website Layout
description: A documentation site's layout: a sticky header with search, a sidebar that's a sticky column from 1024 px and a drawer below, the article at a reading width with code that Copy copies, and a table of contents that marks the section being read without touching the URL.

tokens.note: Suggested defaults. The project's design tokens and existing components win.

layout.layering: Layers, bottom to top: the page, sticky bars, dropdowns and popovers, toasts, then modals, which make the rest of the page inert. The project's layering scale wins; native <dialog> and the popover attribute use the top layer and need no z-index. The header, the sidebar's column, and the table of contents are sticky bars; the drawer and the search dialog are modals.

positioningContract.header: Sticky at the top, as wide as the page; scroll-padding-top at its height
positioningContract.sidebar: From 1024 px, a sticky column below the header that scrolls inside itself; below, a fixed drawer over the page
positioningContract.content: The main element, in a minmax(0, 1fr) column, up to 768 px wide
positioningContract.toc: From 1280 px, a sticky column; below, a collapsed disclosure at the top of the content
positioningContract.footer: After the content, as wide as the page, scrolling with it

invariants: The page scrolls, not a box inside it
scroll-padding-top at the header's height keeps focused elements and link targets clear of the sticky header
The content column is minmax(0, 1fr), so wide code and tables scroll inside themselves
Nothing is position: fixed apart from the drawer and its backdrop below 1024 px

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Build or extend a documentation site: a sticky header with search, a sidebar that's a sticky column from 1024 px and a drawer below with the rest of the page inert, the article with breadcrumbs, code blocks, and callouts, and a table of contents that marks the section being read without touching the URL. Prefer the project's docs framework and search; build on its layout components when it has suitable ones. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: A page grid that scrolls as a page, with sticky header, sidebar, and table of contents, and scroll-padding-top at the header's height
One sidebar nav: a sticky column from 1024 px, a drawer below with the rest of the page inert
Search that prefers the project's own, opened with Cmd+K or Ctrl+K and named by its visible text
A table of contents that marks the section being read, the last short sections included, without history entries
Code blocks that scroll inside themselves, with a Copy button that says whether it worked
Headings with anchor links after them, callouts with text labels, and underlined links
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, the router, the docs framework (Docusaurus, Nextra, VitePress, Starlight, Mintlify), its search, and the existing components (projectDetection). If the project already has a docs layout, configure or extend it to meet this guide instead of building another, and keep its APIs.
2. Choose what the task needs: search, the table of contents, versions, the theme control. Leave out the rest.
3. Lay out the page grid (layoutModel, implementationDetails.grid) and the header (components.Header).
4. Build the sidebar and its drawer below 1024 px (components.Sidebar), as the Sidebar Navigation and Dashboard guides do.
5. Build the article (components.Article): breadcrumbs, headings with anchor links, callouts, and code blocks with Copy (frameworkPatterns.copyCode).
6. Add the table of contents and its scroll spy (components.TableOfContents, frameworkPatterns.scrollSpy).
7. Connect search: the project's own, or a dialog as in implementationDetails.search.
8. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, a phone, 200% zoom, and reduced motion, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

SkipLink.description: The page's first focusable element, going to the main area

Header.description: Sticky: the logo, the main nav, the search button, the theme control, the repository link, and Menu below 1024 px

Sidebar.description: nav "Docs": a sticky column from 1024 px, the drawer below

Backdrop.description: Below 1024 px, behind the open drawer; a click closes the drawer

Main.description: main#main: breadcrumbs, the h1, the article, page meta, previous and next pages

StatusRegion.description: One polite status region, present from the start

Header.description: A skip link to <main id="main" tabindex="-1">, the logo, a <nav> labelled "Main" with the site's sections (Docs, API, Blog), the search button, the theme control, and the repository link. Below 1024 px, a Menu button for the drawer.

behavior.sticky: The page scrolls, not a box inside it. The header sticks to the top, and scroll-padding-top on the root element, set to its height, scrolls focused elements and link targets clear of it (WCAG 2.2 2.4.11); headings need no scroll-margin-top of their own.
behavior.searchButton: The search button's name is its visible text ("Search docs"). It shows its shortcut as "⌘K" on Apple systems and "Ctrl K" elsewhere, with aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K Control+K".
behavior.themeControl: The theme control follows the Dark/Light Mode guide: a button with aria-pressed for two themes, or a radio group or a menu with light, dark, and system for three. A button that cycles through three themes doesn't say what the next press does.
behavior.repositoryLink: The repository link is named "GitHub"; like any link that opens a new tab, it says so ("GitHub, opens in a new tab").

Sidebar.description: One <nav> labelled "Docs", with lists of links. A group is a disclosure: a button with aria-expanded that shows its list; a closed list is hidden, so its links aren't in the Tab order. The Sidebar Navigation guide covers it in full.

behavior.currentPage: The current page's group is open on load, from the URL on the server, and its link has aria-current="page" and looks different by more than color. The current link is scrolled into view in the sidebar on load.
behavior.savedGroups: Saving which other groups are open is optional; if saved, it applies before the first paint, under the app's own prefix (such as acme.docs.groups), or the sidebar jumps after hydration.
behavior.labelsAndKeys: Links wrap; nothing is cut off with an ellipsis. Tab moves through the links; arrow keys between them are an optional extra, as in the APG disclosure navigation example.
behavior.drawer: Below 1024 px, the Menu button (aria-expanded, aria-controls) opens the same <nav> as a drawer over the page. There's no second copy, so no id appears twice. While it's open, everything else is inert (the Modal Dialog guide's model, without a focus-trap library), so focus and screen readers stay in it, and the page behind doesn't scroll. Focus moves to its Close button ("Close menu"); Close, Escape, a click on the backdrop, and a followed link close it, and focus returns to Menu. When the window crosses 1024 px, focus on an element that hides moves to the nearest control that stays: from Menu or Close to the current page's link, from the sidebar to Menu. React to a matchMedia change, not to resize events. The Dashboard guide's drawer snippet does all of this.

Article.description: The page's title is its only <h1>. Text is 16 px at line height 1.7, at most 768 px wide; links in the text are underlined.

behavior.breadcrumbs: Breadcrumbs, when the docs have levels: a <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> with an ordered list, the current page last with aria-current="page", and the separators hidden from screen readers.
behavior.headings: Headings <h2> and <h3> have ids. A heading's anchor link comes after the heading, not inside it, so it doesn't join the heading's name; it's named after it ("Link to Installation"), and shows on focus as well as on hover.
behavior.callouts: Callouts have a text label ("Note", "Warning", "Danger"), visible or visually hidden, besides their color and icon (WCAG 1.4.1).
behavior.variants: Variants of the same code (npm, pnpm, yarn) are tabs, as in the Tabs guide.
behavior.pageMeta: "Last updated" is a <time datetime>; "Edit this page" says so when it opens a new tab. Previous and next pages are links in a <nav aria-label="Pages">, each with its direction and the page's title in its text.
behavior.code: A code block is a <figure>; its file name, if any, is the <figcaption>. A block that scrolls sideways gets tabindex="0", so the keyboard can scroll it, and the page itself never scrolls sideways. Copy copies the code's text and reads "Copied" for a moment; the page's one status region says it too, emptied first, so a second copy is announced again. The clipboard can refuse: navigator.clipboard.writeText was refused in Chromium without the clipboard permission and allowed after a click in Firefox and WebKit (checked). Then Copy says so and selects the code, so the keyboard's copy shortcut works. Line numbers are drawn with CSS counters, or left out of what Copy copies, so screen readers and the clipboard get only the code. Highlighting happens at build time, and every token color meets 4.5:1 against the block's background.

TableOfContents.description: From 1280 px the table of contents is its own column: a <nav> labelled by its heading, "On this page", with links to the page's <h2> and <h3>, sticky below the header and scrolling inside itself. Below 1280 px the same list sits in a collapsed <details> with the summary "On this page" at the top of the content. With fewer than two headings, leave it out.

behavior.scrollSpy: The scroll spy marks the link of the section being read with aria-current="true", and never touches the URL. Setting the URL's hash on every change adds a history entry for each heading and jumps the page, so Back walks through headings; history.replaceState adds none (both checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). A click on a link of the table of contents is a normal link, with one history entry.
behavior.currentHeading: A heading counts once its top passes a line that follows the scroll down to 30% of the window; over the last window of scrolling, the line moves on to the bottom. A fixed band (such as an IntersectionObserver with a root margin of 60 px at the top and 70% at the bottom) misses the first heading, which starts above it, and the last headings of a page whose last sections are short, which never reach it: in a 700 px window, only the second of four headings ever entered it (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit).

Footer.description: Link groups under headings, social links named after their service, and the legal line. It follows the content and is as wide as the page.

desktop.layout: Three columns: the sidebar, the content, the table of contents

tablet.layout: Two columns: the sidebar and the content; the table of contents as a collapsed disclosure at the top of the content

mobile.layout: One column: the content; the sidebar as a drawer opened by Menu; the table of contents as a collapsed disclosure
mobile.content: 16 to 20 px padding; nothing scrolls sideways at 320 px wide

resizeHandling.approach: React to changes of matchMedia('(min-width: 1024px)'), not to resize events: widening closes the drawer, and focus on what hides moves to what stays (components.Sidebar.behavior.drawer).

drawerOpen.description: Whether the drawer is open, below 1024 px.

openGroups.description: The sidebar's open groups; the current page's group is always open on load.
openGroups.persistence: Optional: storage under the app's own prefix (such as acme.docs.groups), applied before the first paint

currentHeading.description: The id of the heading the scroll spy marks.
currentHeading.determination: From the headings' positions, once per frame while scrolling (frameworkPatterns.scrollSpy)

searchOpen.description: Whether the search dialog is open.

ssrConsiderations.sidebar: Render the current page's group open, from the URL; apply saved groups before the first paint.
ssrConsiderations.drawer: Render the drawer closed; it opens only from the browser.
ssrConsiderations.theme: Set the theme before the first paint, as the Dark/Light Mode guide says.

keys.openGroups: acme.docs.groups, where acme stands for the app's own prefix; optional

navigationBehavior.onRouteChange: In a single-page app, a route change updates document.title, moves focus to the new page's <h1> (tabindex="-1") unless the framework announces routes itself, closes the drawer, moves aria-current, and starts the scroll spy on the new headings.
navigationBehavior.inPageLinks: Links to headings land below the header through scroll-padding-top; smooth scrolling only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

rtl.notes: Logical properties (inset-inline-start, margin-inline-end) put the sidebar on the start side and the table of contents on the end side in right-to-left text.

mobileSafeArea.notes: On phones with a notch, env(safe-area-inset-top) pads the header only when the viewport meta tag has viewport-fit=cover.

motionPreferences.prefersReducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the drawer appears without sliding, groups open at once, and links to headings jump.

overflowPolicy.page: No sideways scrolling, down to 320 px wide
overflowPolicy.content: minmax(0, 1fr), so wide content can't widen the page
overflowPolicy.code: Code blocks scroll sideways inside themselves; a scrolling block gets tabindex="0"
overflowPolicy.sidebarAndToc: Each scrolls inside itself when it is taller than the window below the header

requirements.2.5.3: The search button's name is its visible text.
requirements.3.2.2: A version switcher doesn't navigate when its value changes; it's a list of links.
requirements.4.1.3: Copy and search results give their results in one polite status region.

keyboardNavigation.order: The skip link, the header, the sidebar, the main area, the table of contents, and the footer: the order in the page.
keyboardNavigation.search: Cmd+K on Apple systems, Ctrl+K elsewhere, opens search; Escape closes it.
keyboardNavigation.escape: Closes the drawer or the search dialog, with focus back on its button.

pages.aria-label: Pages, on the previous and next links' nav

colorContrast.note: See designSystem.colors; check the project's own colors, and its code theme, the same way.

designSystem.note: Suggested defaults for projects without a design. The project's tokens and existing components win; check its colors meet the same contrast.

light.links: #4f46e5, underlined (6.3:1); also the current section in the table of contents. #6366f1 is only 4.47:1
light.sidebarCurrent: The link in #4f46e5 with a marker on its start side

dark.page: #0a0a0a, with #d4d4d8 text (13.4:1), #a1a1aa muted text (7.7:1), and #fafafa headings (19.0:1)
dark.links: #818cf8, underlined (6.6:1). #71717a is only 4.1:1 for muted text

commonVariations.versions: A version switcher is a disclosure with links, as the Navigation Bar guide's dropdowns are. A <select> that navigates when its value changes changes the context on input (WCAG 3.2.2).
commonVariations.apiReference: A wider content column, or the description and the code side by side from 1280 px, with the table of contents left out.
commonVariations.feedback: "Was this page helpful?" with two buttons that keep their names and use aria-pressed, and the thanks in the status region.

implementationDetails.grid: The page scrolls, not a box inside it. The header sticks to the top, and scroll-padding-top on the root element, set to its height, scrolls focused elements and link targets clear of it (WCAG 2.2 2.4.11); headings need no scroll-margin-top of their own. From 1280 px, three columns: the sidebar (260 px), the content (up to 768 px, in a minmax(0, 1fr) column, so a wide table or code block can't widen the page), and the table of contents (220 px). From 1024 px, two: the sidebar and the content. Below 1024 px, one: the content, with the sidebar as a drawer. The sidebar's column and the table of contents are sticky below the header, as tall as the window minus the header, and scroll inside themselves. A fixed sidebar would cover the start of the footer, which spans the page after the content; a sticky one ends with its column. The header and the footer are as wide as the page (100%), not the viewport's width, which includes the scrollbar on Windows and makes the page scroll sideways.
implementationDetails.search: Prefer the project's existing search: the docs framework's own, DocSearch, or Pagefind. Configure it to meet this guide rather than building another. Otherwise: Cmd+K or Ctrl+K, or the search button, opens a modal dialog with a search field and a list of results, with the APG combobox's keys; Escape closes it, and focus returns to the button. The number of results goes to a polite status region once typing pauses. The Command Palette guide covers it in full.
implementationDetails.layering: Layers, bottom to top: the page, sticky bars, dropdowns and popovers, toasts, then modals, which make the rest of the page inert. The project's layering scale wins; native <dialog> and the popover attribute use the top layer and need no z-index. The header, the sidebar's column, and the table of contents are sticky bars; the drawer and the search dialog are modals.
implementationDetails.appearance: Suggested defaults; the project's design and tokens win. The header is 60 px tall; the sidebar 260 px, the content up to 768 px, the table of contents 220 px; content padding 32 to 48 px, and 16 to 20 px on phones. Light: #ffffff with #1f2937 text (14.7:1), #6b7280 muted text (4.8:1), and #4f46e5 for links and the current section (6.3:1); #6366f1 is only 4.47:1. Dark: #0a0a0a with #d4d4d8 text (13.4:1), #a1a1aa muted text (7.7:1), #fafafa headings (19.0:1), and #818cf8 for links and the current section (6.6:1); #71717a is only 4.1:1. Callouts: a tinted background with a dark label, #1d4ed8 on #eff6ff for a note (6.2:1), #92400e on #fffbeb for a warning (6.8:1), and #991b1b on #fef2f2 for danger (7.6:1). Motion is optional: the drawer slides in over 300 ms, and links to headings scroll smoothly only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference; under reduce, nothing slides.

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

frameworkPatterns.note: Short snippets in plain HTML and JavaScript for the parts that are easiest to get wrong; adapt them to the project's framework and its version. The drawer is the Dashboard guide's drawer snippet; the sidebar's groups are in the Sidebar Navigation guide.

scrollSpy.description: The table of contents' scroll spy: once per frame while scrolling, it marks the link of the last heading past a line that follows the scroll down to 30% of the window and moves on to the bottom over the last window of scrolling; it never touches the URL.

copyCode.description: Copy on a code block: copies the code's text, reads "Copied" for two seconds, says it in the page's status region (emptied first, so a second copy is announced too), and when the clipboard refuses, says so and selects the code.

edgeCases.shortPage: With fewer than two headings, the table of contents is left out and the content takes its space.
edgeCases.longSidebar: It scrolls inside itself, with the current link scrolled into view on load.
edgeCases.deepNesting: Three levels at most in the sidebar; past that, split the section.
edgeCases.print: Hide the header's links, the sidebar, and the table of contents, and let code wrap.
edgeCases.noScript: From 1024 px the sidebar works without it; below, the drawer needs it, so keep the docs reachable without it too, such as from the docs' home page.

must: Use the project's docs framework, search, and layout components when they're suitable, and keep their APIs
Let the page scroll, with a sticky header and scroll-padding-top at its height
Use one sidebar nav for the docked column and the drawer, with the rest of the page inert while the drawer is open
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
mustNot: Add a dependency, such as a search, scroll-spy, or focus-trap library, without asking
Change the URL or add history entries while the page scrolls
Put a heading's anchor link inside the heading, or show it only on hover
Make the sidebar position: fixed from 1024 px, or hide overflow on the content
Cut sidebar or table of contents labels off with an ellipsis
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: The page starts with a skip link, and the header, the sidebar, the main area, the table of contents, and the footer are landmarks; the two navs have different names
The page scrolls, the header sticks, scroll-padding-top keeps a focused link clear of it, and nothing scrolls sideways at 320 px wide
From 1024 px the sidebar is a sticky column; below, Menu opens the same nav as a drawer with a Close button, and the rest of the page is inert
Close, Escape, the backdrop, and a followed link close the drawer, focus returns to Menu, and crossing 1024 px keeps focus on something that shows
The sidebar's groups are disclosure buttons, the current page's group is open on load, and its link has aria-current="page"
The search button is named by its visible text and opens search with Cmd+K on Apple systems and Ctrl+K elsewhere
From 1280 px the table of contents is a sticky column; below, a collapsed "On this page" disclosure at the top of the content; it is left out with fewer than two headings
Scrolling marks the section being read, the last short sections included, adds no history entries, and leaves the URL alone
Each heading's anchor link comes after the heading, is named after it, and shows on focus as well as on hover
Copy copies the code and says "Copied", or says that copying failed and selects the code; a second copy is announced too
A code block that scrolls sideways can be reached with Tab, and line numbers are not part of what Copy copies
Callouts have a text label, such as "Warning", besides their color and icon
Links in the article are underlined, and text meets 4.5:1 in both themes
In a single-page app, a route change updates the title, moves focus to the new page's h1, and closes the drawer
Under reduced motion nothing slides, and links to headings jump instead of scrolling smoothly
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens
